chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

regarding a man who contracted his slave and stipulated a condition upon him that his inheritance would be for him. So that was raised to Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him), so he invalidated his condition and said: 'The Stipulated Condition of Allah is before the stipulation of your condition'.

key_terms.شرط الله: The condition of Allah (referring to the divine mandate of manumission)
key_terms.كاتب: A slave who has entered into a contract to buy his freedom

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a master's condition that a freed slave's inheritance belongs to him?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and reported to Amir al-Mu'minin (AS), establishes the principle of 'tarjih' (preference) where the inherent condition of Allah—manumission—supersedes contractual stipulations. It highlights the jurisprudential maxim that the divine decree of freeing the slave inherently includes the right to inherit, rendering any clause excluding inheritance void. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on the completeness of manumission, ensuring the freed slave achieves full legal and financial independence.
